short_definition: Infamous malware that scanned the internet for IoT devices running factory default passwords to launch DDoS attacks.
layman_explanation: Malware that hijacked thousands of smart security cameras running default passwords to crash major websites.

short_definition: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition architectures used to monitor and control industrial infrastructure.
layman_explanation: The master computer control systems managing power grids, water treatment plants, and factories.

short_definition: Combinations of control components that manage industrial processes in critical infrastructure.
layman_explanation: The specialized computers, switches, and valves that run heavy manufacturing plants and electrical grids.

short_definition: Hardware and software that detects or causes a change through the direct monitoring of physical industrial devices.
layman_explanation: Technology managing physical equipment like factory robotics, valves, and power generators.

short_definition: Security flaws in the low-level embedded software permanently written into an IoT device's hardware.
layman_explanation: A permanent bug in the built-in operating code of a smart thermostat or security camera.

short_definition: An industrial digital computer ruggedized for the control of manufacturing processes or robotic devices.
layman_explanation: A heavy-duty computer chip controlling physical machinery like assembly line belts and water pumps.

short_definition: A famous cyber weapon designed specifically to target industrial PLCs and sabotage nuclear centrifuges.
layman_explanation: A legendary computer virus designed to physically destroy nuclear centrifuges by altering motor speeds.

short_definition: Securing lightweight messaging protocols used by constrained IoT devices to prevent data interception.
layman_explanation: Securing the lightweight communication messages sent between smart home sensors and servers.

short_definition: A specialized web transfer protocol designed for resource-constrained IoT devices.
layman_explanation: A simplified version of HTTP built for tiny smart sensors with limited battery and processing power.

short_definition: Low-power wireless mesh communication standards used in smart home automation.
layman_explanation: The wireless signals that smart lightbulbs and door locks use to talk to each other.

short_definition: A reference architecture modeling network segmentation boundaries between industrial OT and corporate IT.
layman_explanation: A security blueprint separating factory machinery networks from corporate email networks.

short_definition: Administrative credentials permanently baked into IoT firmware by manufacturers that users cannot change.
layman_explanation: Smart cameras leaving factory floors with unchangeable passwords like 'admin123' hardcoded in their chips.

short_definition: Security risks emerging when previously isolated industrial operational networks connect to corporate IT networks.
layman_explanation: Risks created when connecting factory floor machinery directly to office Wi-Fi and the internet.

short_definition: Securing wireless firmware updates sent to smart devices against tampering or interception.
layman_explanation: Ensuring smart cars receive authentic, encrypted software updates wirelessly without hacker interception.

short_definition: Disabling debug ports and unneeded features on single-purpose hardware devices.
layman_explanation: Disabling maintenance test ports on smart meters before shipping them to customers.

short_definition: Connecting directly to physical hardware debugging pins on a circuit board to extract firmware and keys.
layman_explanation: Attaching testing wires directly to a circuit board to extract private encryption keys.

short_definition: Accessing unencrypted serial console interfaces on physical circuit boards to gain root shell access.
layman_explanation: Connecting a cable to exposed pins on a router circuit board to bypass login screens.

short_definition: Measuring fluctuations in an IoT device's electrical power consumption to extract cryptographic keys.
layman_explanation: Measuring subtle electrical power dips on a smart chip to guess its secret encryption keys.

short_definition: Intentionally causing voltage or clock spikes to disrupt processor execution and bypass security checks.
layman_explanation: Zap a microchip with a tiny voltage spike at the exact millisecond it checks a password to bypass authentication.

short_definition: An industrial communication protocol originally designed without encryption or authentication mechanisms.
layman_explanation: An old industrial protocol that sends plain-text commands to factory equipment without password checks.

short_definition: A communications protocol used in process automation systems, particularly in electric and water utilities.
layman_explanation: The protocol power companies use to send status updates and commands between substations.

short_definition: A ruggedized firewall designed for extreme physical environments and industrial protocol inspection.
layman_explanation: A heavy-duty firewall built to handle factory heat and inspect specialized industrial commands.

short_definition: Protecting digital communications and automated control systems powering modern electricity grids.
layman_explanation: Securing automated electrical meters and power distribution grids against blackout attacks.

short_definition: Securing connected healthcare equipment like pacemakers and infusion pumps from cyber tampering.
layman_explanation: Securing hospital equipment like smart IV pumps and heart monitors from cyberattacks.

short_definition: Securing internal Controller Area Network buses in modern vehicles against unauthorized command injection.
layman_explanation: Securing the internal computer wiring in modern cars so hackers cannot tamper with brakes remotely.

short_definition: A malicious modification to an integrated circuit or chip design added during manufacturing.
layman_explanation: A rogue micro-transistor added to a computer chip at the factory to create a physical backdoor.

short_definition: Insecure cloud interfaces managing IoT devices, allowing attackers to control hardware remotely.
layman_explanation: A flaw in a smart lock's web server allowing strangers to unlock your front door over the internet.

short_definition: Securing virtual cloud representations used to store and synchronize IoT device state data.
layman_explanation: Securing the cloud mirror that saves your smart thermostat's settings when it goes offline.

short_definition: Compromising millions of low-power IoT consumer devices to generate record-breaking DDoS floods.
layman_explanation: Combining millions of hacked smart lightbulbs into a botnet to take down major web infrastructure.

short_definition: Securing data processing nodes deployed physically close to local sensors rather than in central clouds.
layman_explanation: Securing the local mini-server installed directly in a factory rather than relying on distant cloud servers.

short_definition: Extracting and analyzing binary image files from IoT hardware to locate hidden credentials and bugs.
layman_explanation: Extracting the code from a smart camera chip to search for hidden passwords and backdoors.

short_definition: A tamper-resistant dedicated hardware chip hosting secure applications and cryptographic keys.
layman_explanation: A mini vault chip inside an IoT device designed to destroy keys if someone tampers with it physically.

short_definition: A unique hardware fingerprint derived from microscopic variations in semiconductor manufacturing.
layman_explanation: A unique silicon fingerprint created by accidental micro-variations during chip manufacturing.

short_definition: Shipping IoT devices with open management ports, unencrypted protocols, and universal passwords.
layman_explanation: Selling smart cameras that arrive out of the box with open Wi-Fi and disabled password prompts.

short_definition: Industrial hardware operating on multi-decade lifecycles lacking basic modern security controls.
layman_explanation: Factory machinery built 30 years ago running without passwords or patch capabilities.

short_definition: Monitoring industrial network traffic without sending active probes that could crash sensitive PLCs.
layman_explanation: Listening silently to factory machine signals without sending test messages that might crash equipment.

short_definition: Dedicated hardware systems engineered to trigger automatic emergency shutdowns during industrial hazards.
layman_explanation: The emergency shutdown systems that automatically vent pressure or turn off gas lines during accidents.

short_definition: Malware designed specifically to manipulate industrial Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS).
layman_explanation: A cyber weapon built specifically to disable emergency safety shutdown systems in industrial facilities.

short_definition: Verifying the integrity of an IoT device's software state before permitting it onto a network.
layman_explanation: Proving a smart sensor is running authentic, untampered firmware before letting it connect to a server.

short_definition: Intercepting unencrypted radio communications passing between smart devices and hubs.
layman_explanation: Listening in on unencrypted radio signals between a smart door sensor and its wall hub.

short_definition: Capturing an unencrypted radio signal (e.g., garage door clicker) and retransmitting it later to trigger the action.
layman_explanation: Recording the radio code sent by your garage door opener and playing it back to open your garage.

short_definition: Jamming and capturing rolling code radio signals to steal valid future unlock codes for cars and gates.
layman_explanation: Jamming your car key signal once so you press it again, letting the attacker steal a valid unlock code.

short_definition: Automated onboarding of IoT devices using secure embedded certificates directly out of the box.
layman_explanation: A smart device connecting securely to its company network automatically the moment you plug it into power.

short_definition: Threats targeting interconnected municipal IoT systems like traffic lights, water distribution, and transit.
layman_explanation: Securing connected city systems like traffic lights and water supply controls against cyber sabotage.

short_definition: Broadcasting fake Bluetooth LE beacon IDs to trick nearby location tracking and indoor navigation systems.
layman_explanation: Broadcasting fake Bluetooth signals to trick retail apps into giving away automated location discounts.

short_definition: Designing hardware cases that erase cryptographic memory if opened or physically manipulated.
layman_explanation: Building a smart meter case that wipes its internal memory if someone tries to pry the cover open.

short_definition: An industrial communication architecture providing integrated encryption and authentication capabilities.
layman_explanation: A modern industrial protocol designed with built-in encryption for factory equipment communications.

short_definition: Managing critical industrial equipment using completely isolated physical network channels.
layman_explanation: Controlling critical factory equipment through a separate cable that is physically disconnected from the main network.

short_definition: Malware engineered to cross isolated networks using infected USB drives, acoustic frequencies, or thermal leaks.
layman_explanation: Malware jumping onto isolated offline computers via infected flash drives or physical acoustic signals.

short_definition: Documenting all open-source libraries and hardware microchips integrated into an IoT device.
layman_explanation: A master parts list revealing every third-party software library and chip installed in a smart device.
